notes: Cross-verse split. The supplied English preposition governing a Greek accusative object goes to the verb in 11.6 (seek after him), 11.10 (looked for the city), 11.14 (seeking after a country) and 11.29 (passed through the sea), but to the pronoun in 11.16 (of them). Nothing in the source licenses the difference: αὐτούς is an accusative object exactly as αὐτόν is at 11.6, and English marks an accusative object with no preposition, so of is not a case helper under rule 21 but the English predicate's own government, which rule 36 leaves with the verb where no Greek preposition stands. t017 moves from αὐτούς into ἐπαισχύνεται's unit; the pronoun stands bare.
